sources.entry: AmuseWiki - Amusewiki is based on the Emacs Muse markup, remaining mostly compatible with the original implementation. It can work as a read-only site, as a moderated wiki, or as a fully open wiki or even as a private site. (Source Code) GPL-1.0 Perl/Docker

summary.one_liner: AmuseWiki is a Perl wiki engine that uses the Text::Amuse markup (based on Emacs Muse) with a Git backend, able to run as a read-only site, moderated wiki, open wiki, or private site.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a wiki engine built on the Text::Amuse markup, which is based on and mostly compatible with Emacs Muse, with a Git backend. It can operate as a read-only site, a moderated wiki, a fully open wiki, or a private site. A single instance can host multiple sites. The application is written in Perl and uses the AmuseWikiFarm namespace, a legacy name from its predecessor. The README points to external documentation covering install and upgrade, site setup, customization, user roles, SSL certificates, editing with the Muse markup, offline editing with Git, and localization. The README body itself contains mostly links, which did not survive extraction, so specific features beyond these are not detailed here.
use_cases: host a multi-site wiki from one instance
set up a private wiki for a group
publish a read-only documentation site from Muse files
edit wiki pages offline with Git
how_to_run: See the official documentation for install and upgrade instructions
Docker images are available; see the Docker link in the README
notable: Supports read-only, moderated, open, and private wiki modes
Hosts multiple independent sites on one instance
Uses Text::Amuse markup, mostly compatible with Emacs Muse
Git backend, with offline editing via Git
caveats: README warns not to run make test in the production directory, since tests leave many files behind
Documentation is hosted externally and may be offline; README points to GitHub source files as a fallback
